sections.skill: Set up and complete an argument by contradiction

questions.prompt: In a proof by contradiction, you assume the statement is false and show that this leads to something impossible. To prove "there is no largest even integer" by contradiction, how should the proof begin?

choices.text: Show that 100 is an even integer.
Assume there is a largest even integer; call it N.
Assume there is no largest even integer.
Assume every even integer is less than 100.

questions.correct_answer: Assume there is a largest even integer; call it N.

questions.prompt: Definitions: an integer n is even if n = 2k for some integer k, and odd if n = 2k + 1 for some integer k. An integer n is a multiple of m if n = mk for some integer k. In a proof by contradiction, you assume the statement is false and show that this leads to something impossible. Put the steps of a proof that if n squared is even, then n is even, in order.

items.text: Assume n squared is even, but n is odd.
Then n = 2k + 1 for some integer k.
So n squared = 2(2k squared + 2k) + 1, which is odd.
This contradicts n squared being even, so n must be even.

questions.correct_answer: Assume n squared is even, but n is odd. → Then n = 2k + 1 for some integer k. → So n squared = 2(2k squared + 2k) + 1, which is odd. → This contradicts n squared being even, so n must be even.

sections.skill: Strategy: assume the opposite and look for the impossible
sections.relationship: Students start a contradiction proof by assuming the wrong thing. Writing the exact opposite first, and then hunting for a clash, gives every such proof the same shape.
sections.author_note: Students start a contradiction proof by assuming the wrong thing. Writing the exact opposite first, and then hunting for a clash, gives every such proof the same shape.

lesson.title: Assume the opposite and look for the impossible
text: Write the exact opposite (negation) of what you want to prove, and assume it.
Reason from that assumption with definitions and facts you know.
Stop when you reach something impossible, such as 1 = 0 or a number that is both even and odd. Then the assumption is false, so the statement is true.

example.title: Worked example (a different claim)
prompt: Prove: there is no smallest positive fraction.
steps: Assume the opposite: there is a smallest positive fraction r.
Then r / 2 is also a positive fraction, and r / 2 < r.
That contradicts r being smallest, so no smallest positive fraction exists.

questions.prompt: In a proof by contradiction, you assume the statement is false and show that this leads to something impossible. To prove that no integers a and b satisfy 6a + 9b = 10, which fact gives the contradiction?

choices.text: 6a + 9b = 3(2a + 3b) is a multiple of 3, but 10 is not.
a and b would have to be fractions.
10 is even, and 6a + 9b is always odd.

questions.correct_answer: 6a + 9b = 3(2a + 3b) is a multiple of 3, but 10 is not.

questions.prompt: In a proof by contradiction, you assume the statement is false and show that this leads to something impossible. Put the steps of the proof that the square root of 2 is not a fraction in order.

items.text: Assume the square root of 2 = p / q, with p and q integers in lowest terms.
Then p squared = 2q squared, so p squared is even, so p is even: p = 2m.
Then 4m squared = 2q squared, so q squared = 2m squared, and q is even.
Both p and q are even, which contradicts lowest terms.

questions.correct_answer: Assume the square root of 2 = p / q, with p and q integers in lowest terms. → Then p squared = 2q squared, so p squared is even, so p is even: p = 2m. → Then 4m squared = 2q squared, so q squared = 2m squared, and q is even. → Both p and q are even, which contradicts lowest terms.

questions.prompt: In a proof by contradiction, you assume the statement is false and show that this leads to something impossible. Assume there are only finitely many primes, p1, p2, ..., pk, and let N = p1 x p2 x ... x pk + 1. Why is this a contradiction?

choices.text: N is always an even number.
N is always a prime number.
N is larger than every prime, so N is not prime.
N leaves remainder 1 when divided by each listed prime, so a prime factor of N is not on the list.

questions.correct_answer: N leaves remainder 1 when divided by each listed prime, so a prime factor of N is not on the list.

questions.prompt: 2 x 3 x 5 x 7 x 11 x 13 + 1 is a prime number.

In a proof by contradiction, you assume the statement is false and show that this leads to something impossible. Put the steps of a proof that if a + b is at least 20, then a is at least 10 or b is at least 10, in order.

items.text: Assume a + b is at least 20, but a < 10 and b < 10.
Adding the two inequalities gives a + b < 20.
That contradicts a + b being at least 20.
So a is at least 10 or b is at least 10.

questions.correct_answer: Assume a + b is at least 20, but a < 10 and b < 10. → Adding the two inequalities gives a + b < 20. → That contradicts a + b being at least 20. → So a is at least 10 or b is at least 10.

questions.prompt: In a proof by contradiction, you assume the statement is false and show that this leads to something impossible. Claim: every integer is even. "Proof: Assume some integer is odd, say 3. Then 3 = 2k for no integer k. Contradiction." What is wrong?

choices.text: Nothing impossible was reached; 3 not being 2k agrees with 3 being odd.
It should assume that every integer is odd.

questions.correct_answer: Nothing impossible was reached; 3 not being 2k agrees with 3 being odd.
